concept_html:
Power BI separates three layers. Keep them apart in your head.

  • Data lives in tables at the source, such as Delta tables in a lakehouse.
  • A semantic model describes that data for analysis: which tables it uses, how they relate, and which calculations exist.
  • A report holds pages of visuals, such as charts and tables, that query the model.

Tables and relationships. A model usually has a fact table, one row per event or response, holding numbers and keys, and dimension tables that describe those keys, such as region or brand. A relationship links each dimension to the fact table, one-to-many, so a filter on a region narrows the facts to that region. Lesson C6-L1 builds this properly as a star schema.

Columns and measures. A calculated column is worked out once per row and stored. A measure is worked out when a visual asks, for whatever the visual currently shows. That difference matters for ratios:

Weighted reach % = DIVIDE ( SUM ( fact[reach] ), SUM ( fact[base] ) )

This measure divides two totals, so it is right at every level: a region, a wave or everything. An average of per-row percentages weights a row with 2 respondents the same as a row with 2,000.

Filter context. Each visual cell evaluates a measure under the filters that apply to it: slicers, the row and column headers, and page filters. The same measure gives North's figure in North's row and the total in the total row. Lesson C6-L2 shows how to change that context on purpose.

DIVIDE returns blank when the denominator is 0 or blank.

Storage modes. Import copies the data into the model and refreshes it on a schedule. DirectQuery sends each query to the source. Direct Lake (GA in Fabric) reads Delta tables in OneLake directly, without an import copy (lesson C6-L3).

recap.back: Data sits in source tables. The model describes tables, relationships and measures. Reports hold visuals that query the model.
A column is worked out per row and stored. A measure is worked out when a visual asks, in that visual's filter context.
A measure dividing totals: DIVIDE ( SUM ( reach ), SUM ( base ) ). Never average per-row percentages.
Import copies and refreshes. DirectQuery queries the source each time. Direct Lake (GA) reads OneLake Delta tables directly.

title: Power BI basics, reports, semantic models and measures
why_html: A dashboard showed "average reach %" as the average of a calculated column, reach divided by base for each region-wave row. Small regions counted as much as large ones, and the national figure read 70% where the true weighted reach was 83%. A measure dividing the summed reach by the summed base gives 83% at every level, including the total row.
